extracted.intended_audience: NIH grant applicants, NIH grantees, institutional grants administrators, and program officers
extracted.subtask_description: Terms, conditions, and procedural requirements that govern NIH grant applications, awards, administration, allowable costs, human subjects protections, reporting, and closeout. Designed to inform applicants and recipients how to prepare, manage, and close out NIH-funded projects in compliance with federal and NIH-specific requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of Grant Award (NGA)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Notice of Grant Award (Notice of Award) documents the federal award and specifies funding, budget, and additional terms and conditions that apply to the grant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NGA is the official, legally binding notice; it includes period of support, authorized budget, any additional award-specific terms, and references to the NIHGPS. Changes to the award typically require modification of the NGA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding Principles
rubrics_metrics.description: General principles NIH uses to make funding decisions and administer awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes use of peer review results, programmatic priorities, availability of funds, and statutory/regulatory constraints. Grantees must understand how funding decisions were made and abide by funding limitations and conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Which entities and individuals are eligible to apply for and receive NIH grants, with definitions for terms like 'state government', 'small business', 'domestic vs. foreign institution', etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility varies by mechanism (e.g., R01, SBIR, training awards) and program announcement; verify specific FOA and mechanism. Some awards (e.g., construction, fellowships, SBIR/STTR) have unique eligibility rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application Submission Procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedural requirements and required forms for submitting grant applications to NIH, including receipt points, deadlines, and confidentiality of application information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the specified application forms and instructions, meet deadlines and receipt points, and understand legal implications and confidentiality policies. Noncompliant applications may be rejected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer Review Process
rubrics_metrics.description: The scientific/technical merit review (peer review) and subsequent programmatic review steps used to evaluate applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes roles of SRAs, review groups, review criteria, scoring, and how review outcomes influence funding decisions. Applicants should address review criteria clearly in applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Just-in-Time Procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH request for additional information (e.g., human subjects assurances, IACUC approvals, other approvals) prior to award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must provide requested information promptly; failure to provide required JIT materials can delay or prevent funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost Principles and Allowability of Costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Principles that determine which costs are allowable, allocable, reasonable, and consistently treated under NIH awards (linked to OMBCirculars/Cost Principles).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes guidance on direct vs. F&A (indirect) costs, selected items of cost, unallowable costs, cost transfers, overruns, and allocation of costs. Grantees must follow applicable federal cost principles (e.g., OMB A-21/A-87/A-122 as applicable).

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct Costs and Facilities & Administrative (F&A) Costs
rubrics_metrics.description: How to identify and charge direct costs versus facilities and administrative (indirect) costs to NIH grants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes institutional base salary definition, treatment of shared costs, and procedures for reimbursement of F&A; documentation must support direct cost charges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowable and Unallowable Costs / Selected Items of Cost
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific items that are explicitly allowable or unallowable under NIH awards (e.g., salaries, travel, supplies, equipment, entertainment, alcohol).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH provides examples and special rules (e.g., student compensation, clinical care costs). Some items require prior approval or special justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budgeting and Rebudgeting / Significant Rebudgeting
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements for preparing the budget and rules/thresholds for rebudgeting between budget categories or activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Significant rebudgeting requires prior approval; thresholds and definitions provided. Grantees must request prior approval when rebudgeting would change the aims or approved conduct of the project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior-Approval Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Activities and changes that require NIH prior approval (e.g., change in scope, transfer of performance site, personnel changes, rebudgeting above thresholds).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists procedures for requesting prior approval, documentation required, and timelines. Failure to obtain required approvals may result in disallowance or enforcement actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payments and Cash Management (SMARTLINK II/ACH, CASHLINE/ACH)
rubrics_metrics.description: Mechanisms and rules governing payment methods to grantees, cash requests, advances, and interest earned on advances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grantees must follow cash management systems and promptly reconcile and report use of funds; interest earned on advances may require remittance or adjustment per federal rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program Income
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition and treatment of program income generated under NIH awards and how it affects project budgets and reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH specifies whether program income is to be added to the project, deducted from costs, or used to further project objectives; grantees must account for and report program income.

rubrics_metrics.name: Property and Equipment Management Standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for acquisition, management, use, disposal, and recordkeeping of tangible personal property and equipment purchased under NIH awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes property inventory requirements, title to equipment, disposition at closeout, and special rules for transfer or sale. Institutions must maintain adequate property management systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procurement System Standards and Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for procurement systems used to obtain goods and services under NIH awards, including competition, documentation, and allowable contractor arrangements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirements include competition, procurement procedures, use of federal procurement regulations where applicable, and documentation to demonstrate reasonableness and allowability of costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial Management System Standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards that financial management systems must meet (e.g., ability to account for funds, produce accurate reports, and track expenditures by award).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systems must provide reliable, traceable records; permit reconciliation to SF-272/269/425 reports; and support audits and monitoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring and Reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Ongoing monitoring responsibilities and reporting requirements (financial, progress, final reports) that grantees must satisfy during the award and at closeout.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes types and timing of reports (e.g., Financial Status Reports, progress reports), requirements for timely submission, and consequences for delinquent reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record Retention and Access
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements for retention of financial, programmatic, and participant records and providing federal access for audit and review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies retention periods, conditions for access by NIH, HHS, and auditors, and records to be retained after closeout; failure to retain records can lead to enforcement actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audit Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal audit requirements applicable to grantees, including single audit requirements for non-Federal entities and criteria for audit scope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Audits must be performed per OMB Circular A-133 (or successor) and applicable audit standards; audit findings must be addressed and can trigger enforcement actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enforcement Actions, Suspension, Termination, and Withholding of Support
rubrics_metrics.description: Authorities and procedures NIH may use to enforce award terms, including suspension, termination, withholding support, recovery of funds, and other remedies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes grounds for enforcement (noncompliance, misuse of funds, research misconduct), notice and appeal procedures, and actions such as disallowance, suspension, termination, or recovery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventions, Patents, and Rights in Data (Bayh-Dole/Technology Transfer)
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements for handling inventions, patent rights, and rights in data arising from NIH-funded research, including reporting, election to retain title, and commercialization expectations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grantees must comply with Bayh-Dole Act rules, report inventions timely, protect and commercialize inventions in the public interest, and follow NIH data/publication and copyright policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sharing of Research Data
rubrics_metrics.description: Policies and expectations for sharing research data produced with NIH funds, including data sharing plans where required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH encourages timely sharing of data; some FOAs require a data-sharing plan. Guidance covers de-identification, repository submission, and access conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sharing of Unique Research Resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Expectations for making unique research resources (e.g., cell lines, model organisms, reagents) generated with NIH funds broadly available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policies expect resource sharing unless constrained; grantees should include sharing plans and comply with material transfer standards and intellectual property obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human Subjects Protections
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements to protect rights and welfare of human research participants, including IRB review, informed consent, confidentiality, and compliance with DHHS regulations (45 CFR 46).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes procedures for IRB approvals, continuing review, documentation, special protections for vulnerable populations, and requirements for data confidentiality (Privacy Rule).

rubrics_metrics.name: Data and Safety Monitoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements for monitoring clinical research and other human-subjects research to ensure safety and data integrity (e.g., DSMBs for multi-site clinical trials).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires appropriate monitoring commensurate with risk; for clinical trials, may require a Data and Safety Monitoring Board and a monitoring plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigational New Drug (IND) and Investigational Device Exemption (IDE) Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements when clinical research involves investigational drugs or devices, including FDA IND/IDE submissions and compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigators and institutions must ensure appropriate regulatory approvals and compliance with FDA requirements where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion Policies (Women, Minorities, and Children)
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH requirements to include women, minorities, and children in clinical research unless justified otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications must address inclusion plans, recruitment strategies, and statistical approaches to ensure appropriate representation; exceptions require scientific justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human Embryonic Stem Cell (hESC) Research Policy
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH criteria and restrictions governing research using human embryonic stem cells.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only eligible hESC lines may be used; applications must comply with NIH stem cell eligibility and documentation requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Animal Welfare
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements to ensure humane care and use of vertebrate animals in research, including IACUC approvals and compliance with PHS Policy on Humane Care and Use of Laboratory Animals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grantees must have approved animal care protocols, provide training, and ensure appropriate facilities and oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial Conflict of Interest (FCOI)
rubrics_metrics.description: Policies requiring disclosure and management of investigators' significant financial interests that could affect research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions must have FCOI policies, disclose investigator interests to NIH when required, and mitigate/manage conflicts to protect research integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Misconduct
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH policies for responding to allegations of fabrication, falsification, and plagiarism, and requirements for institutional inquiry and reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions must have research misconduct policies, investigate allegations, notify NIH of findings, and take corrective actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Debarment and Suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: Criteria and procedures for excluding individuals or organizations from federal programs due to performance or integrity issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH may refuse to enter into or may terminate awards with debarred/suspended parties; grantees must certify they are not debarred/suspended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drug-Free Workplace and Limitations on Certain Uses of Funds
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements for maintaining a drug-free workplace and prohibitions or limits on use of grant funds for certain activities (e.g., promoting legalization of controlled substances).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grantees must certify compliance, implement related policies, and not use funds for prohibited purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lobbying Restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Restrictions on use of federal funds for lobbying activities and requirements to disclose lobbying in certain circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grantees must not use NIH funds for lobbying and must follow federal lobbying disclosure rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Civil Rights and Non-Discrimination Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Obligations to comply with civil rights statutes including nondiscrimination on the basis of race, sex, age, disability, and limited English proficiency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grantees must ensure equal access and nondiscriminatory practices in programs and services supported by NIH funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privacy and Confidentiality (FOIA, Privacy Act, Confidentiality)
rubrics_metrics.description: Policies governing disclosure of information, FOIA/Privacy Act considerations, and protection of confidential/proprietary information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grantees must understand what information may be publicly disclosed and how to request confidential treatment for proprietary material, and must comply with privacy regulations for identifiable data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of Information and Acknowledgment of Federal Funding
rubrics_metrics.description: Expectations for public access to certain funded research information and requirements to acknowledge NIH funding in publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publications and other products should acknowledge NIH support; certain datasets and results may be subject to public access policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for Construction Grants (Design, Environmental, Safety)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific design, environmental, procurement, and administrative requirements applicable to NIH-assisted construction and alteration grants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes NEPA compliance, flood insurance, historic preservation, seismic safety, accessibility (architectural barriers), procurement for construction services, and relocation assistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conference Grants (Support of Scientific Meetings)
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligibility, allowable/unallowable costs, application requirements, and reporting obligations for NIH conference grants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH defines allowable costs for meetings, requires compliance with public policy requirements, and may impose limits on certain costs; intellectual property/public disclosure rules apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consortium Agreements
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements for agreements between the prime awardee and consortium/contract organizations, including written agreements and responsibilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consortium agreements must delineate administrative and financial responsibilities, prior approvals for subawards, property accountability, and audit requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grants to Foreign Institutions and Foreign Components
rubrics_metrics.description: Special eligibility, administrative, and policy requirements when NIH grants have foreign components or are awarded to foreign institutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes restrictions on allowable costs, reporting, audit, and compliance with U.S. policies where applicable; prior approval may be required for substantial foreign components.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grants to Federal Institutions and Payments to Federal Employees
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for awards to federal institutions or payments made to or on behalf of federal employees under grants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special eligibility and payment rules apply, including VA-university affiliations, allowable costs, procurement, and property accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grants to For-Profit Organizations and SBIR/STTR Programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Special terms for awards to for-profit entities, including allowable costs, profit/fee, and SBIR/STTR program requirements and differences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes rules for indirect costs, independent R&D costs, profit, program income, eligibility (phases), place of performance, and intellectual property expectations for small business programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Patient Care Costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Policy and allowable cost rules for patient care costs incurred as part of research activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines patient care costs, how to compute research patient care costs, F&A treatment, and special procedures for certain hospitals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ruth L. Kirschstein National Research Service Awards (NRSA) — Fellowships and Training Grants
rubrics_metrics.description: Special terms for NRSA individual fellowships and institutional training grants including eligibility, stipend levels, allowable costs, payback, and reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers application requirements, initiation and period of support, full-time/part-time training, stipend supplementation rules, leave, transfers, reporting, and payback obligations for certain trainees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modular Applications and Awards
rubrics_metrics.description: Simplified budget format and administrative procedures for modular budget applications and awards (where applicable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies when modular budgets apply, budget preparation instructions, checklists, and post-award administration for modular grants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Closeout and Final Reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures and requirements for closeout of NIH awards, including submission of final progress and financial reports and disposition of property and data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grantees must submit final reports timely, reconcile expenditures, resolve audit findings, and comply with disposition instructions for equipment and data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant Appeals Procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedural rights and mechanisms for applicants or grantees to appeal NIH administrative actions relating to grants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies grounds, timelines, and processes for appeals of adverse administrative decisions (not scientific peer review outcomes), including designated appeals offices and required documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection and Use of Support Mechanisms
rubrics_metrics.description: Descriptions of NIH support mechanisms (award instruments) and guidance on which mechanisms are appropriate for different types of projects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes R-series, P-series, K-series, fellowships, training grants, cooperative agreements, contracts; applicants should select the mechanism matching program goals and eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sources of Information about NIH Grants Process
rubrics_metrics.description: Where applicants and grantees can find guidance, contacts, and resources (e.g., NIH Guide for Grants and Contracts; eRA; program officers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grantees must monitor NIH Guide for policy changes and contact appropriate program and grants management staff for questions; Part III lists points of contact.
